prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2600 covers a strictly larger slice of the same close()-cleanup problem: it also clears _requestToStreamMapping (which #2692 never touches and which otherwise leaks every closed session's request-id correlations for the life of the process) and fixes the send()/storeEvent() race where a send() suspended in eventStore.storeEvent() across a close() resumes against an already-retired correlation. Both PRs rewrite the same close() lines to settle parked JSON-response-mode POSTs (404 'Session not found' in #2600 vs. JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' in #2692), so they cannot both land without a manual merge conflict on that block. #2692's per-stream batching and 'reuse an already-settled response' handling for that specific sub-case are worth carrying over as a follow-up refinement on top of #2600, but #2600 is the safer base since dropping it would leave the _requestToStreamMapping leak and the storeEvent race unfixed.

clusters.pick_reason: 2763's changeset explicitly covers both halves of the bug — capping the initial arm to min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout) for the no-progress case, and re-arming progress resets against the remaining budget — while 2817 only touches the progress-reset path (adding an `info.startTime` update) and leaves the no-progress hang (the case the changeset calls out: `{timeout:1000, maxTotalTimeout:150}` waiting the full 1000ms) unaddressed. 2763 also ships a changeset file documenting the package bumps; 2817's diff has no changeset. Both PRs touch the same _setupTimeout/reset block in protocol.ts, so merging both would conflict.

members.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: protocol.ts's request-timeout logic fails to treat maxTotalTimeout as a hard ceiling: the timer that governs a pending request is armed/re-armed using only the per-request `timeout` value, so maxTotalTimeout is not honored either on initial arm or on progress-triggered resets. (2 PRs)
